note: Confirms which student this token belongs to. Read the identity guard's output before trusting anything below it.
Whether a student can enumerate the course. Expected to be denied.
Whether a student can see the Vocareum-managed group they are in.
Whether the workspace root is readable at all, which is the cheapest test of the workspace-access entitlement.
What the student sees on entry. Databricks filters this to what they may see, so a short list is not a small workspace.
Whether the student can see the compute user_setup.sh gave them. An empty list here with a cluster visible to the service principal means a missing grant.
Bounds which Spark connector builds a course can install.
Needed only if the student creates their own cluster rather than attaching to one.
Names a cluster that does not exist. NOT_FOUND_OR_HIDDEN here proves nothing on its own; it is in the list to confirm the verdict is reachable.
Whether the student can see the policy that caps what they can spend.
Whether the student can confirm the Spark connector is installed, which is the first thing they will ask when a connector call fails.
Whether the student can see a scope holding an external service's credentials. Seeing the scope is not reading the secret, and a course that connects out needs the second.
METASTORE_NOT_ASSIGNED here explains every Unity Catalog denial below it.
Whether the student can reach the tables the course reads from Databricks.
Only needed for a course that writes to cloud storage directly.
Only needed for a course that runs something on a schedule.
Only needed for a course that queries through SQL rather than a notebook.
Whether the student can mint the token this run is using. If this is denied, the token was made another way and the next operator cannot repeat the measurement.
Whether personal access tokens are enabled for the workspace at all.
